Bind objects into an environment and keep them fresh

Source: R/refresh.R
keep_fresh.Rd

Makes objects that look like ordinary variables but always hold an up-to-date value, built only when it's first needed. Use it for data that lives elsewhere (e.g. a download) and changes occasionally: users keep writing pkg::my_data and get the current version without calling a function.

Usage

keep_fresh(
  checker,
  setters,
  env,
  cache = cachem::cache_mem(),
  state = state_memory(),
  check = "session",
  snapshot_path = NULL,
  snapshot_names = NULL
)

Arguments

checker

function function(state) returning a version key (any R object, compared with identical()). state is the state store, so the checker can remember things between checks (e.g. to skip expensive remote checks).

setters

list Named list of function(key), each returning the value for that name at version key.

env

environment Environment (or unlocked namespace) to create the bindings in.

cache

cachem A cachem cache, such as cachem::cache_mem() (the default; values last for the session) or cachem::cache_disk() (values persist across sessions). Any object with get(), set(), and exists() methods in the cachem style works.

state

FreshState Where checker keeps its state: state_memory() (the default) or state_file() to persist it across sessions. Kept separate from cache so cache eviction can't erase it.

check

character(1) or numeric(1) When to run checker(): "session" (once per keep_fresh() call, i.e. once per package load), "access" (every access), or a number of seconds between checks.

snapshot_path

character(1) Optional snapshot folder (see $save_snapshot()). If supplied, values are read from it instead of the checker and setters until $use_snapshot(NULL).

snapshot_names

character Named vector mapping binding names to object names in snapshots, for bindings whose snapshot object has a different name. Unlisted bindings use their own name.

Value

FreshHandle An R6 object (invisibly) with key() (the current version key), refresh() (re-run the checker now), invalidate() (re-run the checker on the next access), reset() (forget in-session values and checker state; the cache is untouched), set_cache(cache) (switch to another cachem cache; values already loaded this session are kept), save_snapshot(dir, names, packages, key, metadata) (write a hard copy of the values), use_snapshot(dir, check_packages = TRUE) (read values from a hard copy; NULL to stop), cache (the current cachem object), state (the state store), and snapshot (the snapshot in use, or NULL).

Details

Supply a checker that reports which version of the data is current, and one setter per object that builds that object for a given version. Call keep_fresh() from your package's .onLoad() with env set to the package namespace, and export the objects with fresh_exports(). Values are stored in cache, so a setter only runs again when checker reports a new version.

The cache is a standard cachem object, so you (and your users) can choose its location, size limits, and age limits, inspect it, or prune it with the usual cachem methods. Packages that use keep_fresh() should let users supply their own cache (e.g. via an option) and expose the handle's cache so it's never hidden.
